scope: Boundary selection, local footnotes, structural completeness, and visible source anomalies. Not a scholarly certification of translation or transcription accuracy.

groups.reason: The notes for I.1–3 occur after I.4; keep the opening account of family influences with all four corresponding notes.
The notes for Sextus, Alexander, and Fronto in I.9–11 occur after I.13; preserve the intervening section and all matching notes in one contiguous reading.
II.4 opens by referring to putting off these things; II.3 supplies the preceding principles about nature, providence, and using the time available.
III.10 refers to these few principles and III.11 to the aids already mentioned; III.9 supplies the faculty of judgment and its principles.
IV.9 is a single sentence with an unspecified this; IV.10 supplies the fuller account of happenings, universal justice, and responding well.
IV.14 supplies the context of mortality and return to the whole for IV.15’s brief, otherwise unexplained image of grains of frankincense falling at different times.
IV.26 opens by directing attention from those things to these; IV.25 supplies the preceding example of a good life, followed by practical examples in IV.26.
IV.28 is a bare list of defective characters; IV.29 supplies the accompanying account of separation from reason, society, and the universe.

V.15 refers to these things without naming external possessions; V.12 supplies the contrast between virtue and wealth, luxury, and fame, followed by the intervening account of material things and reason.
V.17 leaves the bad person’s action unspecified; the following connected reflections lead to V.20’s explicit example of another person obstructing one’s acts and explain the response.
The translator’s note after V.28 explicitly explains the corrupt or incomplete opening of V.29; keep the section with that note as well as V.29’s own note.
V.35’s this is left unspecified; V.34 supplies the distinction between one’s just acts and matters outside one’s control that grounds the concluding question.

notes: AI editorial review read all 196 sections in books I–VI: I 17; II 17; III 16; IV 51; V 36; VI 59. All unspecified sections should remain singleton readings; no numbered section should be split.

Footnote references [A]–[E] were inspected and counted against indented note definitions. The only references whose definitions fall in a later section in books I–VI are I.1–4 and I.9–13, covered by merges. V.28 also has a note discussing V.29 despite the later section having its own [A] note.

Book I repeats From ... without a complete verb in several sections. Its opening translator note acknowledges that grammatical form; preserve it. The headings and named influences make later numbered sections intelligible without inventing introductory wording.

Preserve source uncertainty markers (+), brackets, ellipses, transliterated Greek, and translator comments. In particular I.16–17, V.28–29, and V.36 explicitly acknowledge corrupt or incomplete underlying passages. Adjacency cannot resolve every uncertainty.

Literal publisher illustration placeholders occur within the section slices at IV.20 and V.8. They are source text and must not silently disappear if the extraction contract is exact contiguous slices.

Suspected transcription anomalies require transparent documentation rather than edits: V.15 contains who snowed; V.29 contains when them art gone out; VI.41 contains thou wilt not blame the gods, and hate men too. The last may materially alter the argument. This review does not establish what a printed edition or Greek witness says.

Some cross-references point outside the reading (for example to other books or the prefatory Life). These are the original scholarly references and are not broken local footnotes; retain them without moving or rewriting text.
All text was reviewed only for grouping, local note attachment, and obvious anomalies. This is not a scholarly certification of translation accuracy or a full comparison with a printed edition.

notes: Read all 291 numbered sections in Books VII–XII: VII 1–75, VIII 1–61, IX 1–42, X 1–38, XI 1–39, XII 1–36. This is structural completeness within the downloaded source, not verification against a historical printed edition.

Applied a mechanical check to every proposed group and default singleton: the counts of [A]–[Z] references equal their corresponding definition counts within each reading. The regex includes unindented footnote definitions in VII45.

Default to one numbered section except the listed merges. Variable length is intentional: for example VII75 contains a very long translator note and XI18 is a long ten-part argument; neither should be split merely for length.
Book IX21 includes the literal illustration placeholder [Illustration: THE FORUM] after the section text. Keep it under exact-source fidelity rather than silently deleting it.
Book X26 contains the reference (vii. 85), but Book VII has only 75 sections. Preserve and flag this source discrepancy; do not silently correct it.
Book XII12 contains the unusual reference string (ii. 11, 12, 13; vii. 62; 18 viii. 17). Preserve it as found.

Apparent typographic defects include IX34 pool souls, VIII45 comformably, XI10 art Now, XI15 What are thou, and XI18 nattering men. They are source features requiring preservation, not automatic spelling correction.

Some source passages explicitly mark textual uncertainty or loss: VII24, VII31, VII58, VII75, VIII35, IX28, IX39, X7, X9, XI18, and XII17. In particular VII58 ends with an ellipsis and an explanation that the conclusion is corrupt; XII17 ends with an incomplete bracketed phrase and an explanatory note. Adjacent-section grouping cannot restore missing ancient text.

XI28 refers to what Socrates said without supplying his words, and XI30–32 are terse literary excerpts without a self-contained argument. Their immediate neighbors do not provide the missing context. Preserve them as original fragments and disclose that an AI boundary review cannot guarantee every original entry is independently intelligible. Do not invent connective text or conflate the different quotations.

Page-based references such as VII9 p. 42, IX3 p. 76 and X38 p. 72 point to the edition’s introductory material. The frozen complete ebook retains that material but these references should not be presented as modern web navigation.

Preserve literal markers such as + for textual uncertainty, [Greek: ...] transliterations, bracketed translator additions, underscores, repeated hyphens, line indentation, and original line endings. Rendering as ordinary Markdown could renumber section starts or interpret source underscores, so source-preserving rendering needs validation.

Book XII27 completes its thought and its note; XII28–36 are present, and XII36 finishes with Depart then satisfied, for he also who releases thee is satisfied. This avoids the known MIT truncation without combining different sources.
